//verify: THROUGH THE WRAPPER, NEVER `dotnet build` (WORK-ISOLATION-PLAN D-6). A bare dotnet
build reports a locked output file as `Build FAILED` with ten screens of MSB3026 --
the exact false diagnosis CLAUDE.md 1 mandates the wrapper to prevent, and it arrives
here when NOBODY IS WATCHING: this runs inside the daemon, during a land.
It runs in the TICKET'S OWN WORKTREE now, on the result of merging main in, BEFORE the
ref moves (REVIEW-AND-MERGE-PLAN R1/D-R1). It used to run after the fast-forward, in
the repository that had just changed, so a red verify had already shipped.
`build` FIRST is not optional: a ticket worktree is a fresh checkout that has never
been built, and `dev test`/`dev gate` REFUSE an absent build output rather than testing
the previous binary (P1.5). D-6 says the step becomes `dev gate`; measured, `dev gate`
alone in a fresh worktree refuses every land with `has never been built`.
WHY THE SUBSET AND NOT THE FULL GATE -- measured on this machine 2026-08-20, in a cold
worktree: `dev build` 2.5s then `dev gate` 273.1s (suites 259.3s), 275.6s total, versus
~17s for `dev test unit m1 m2`. The daemon's control pipe is SERIAL (one server
instance, HandleAsync awaited inline), and the land runs on it -- so the full gate makes
the daemon answer nothing for four and a half minutes on every land: no UI, no lane
input, no `say`. That is CLAUDE.md 0.1's `never hung` violated by 4.6 minutes, so the
full gate cannot go here until the land stops blocking the pipe. Answering REVIEW-AND-
MERGE-PLAN 11's open question with the number rather than a preference; widen this line
the moment the land is asynchronous, and see that plan's 11 for the recommendation.
//autoPublish: The daemon compares `git rev-parse main` against the commit the running build was
made from, and when they differ it builds THAT COMMIT -- in a detached worktree of
its own, never anybody's live tree -- and swaps itself to it. Operator's standing
order: live updates are not sometimes. A failed build changes nothing and announces
loudly; a parked swap offers the usual three answers; three consecutive failures
and it surrenders, once, out loud.
ONLY main publishes itself (RECOVERY-PHASES D-1). Uncommitted work cannot reach the
app at all -- trial it deliberately with `dodona publish --from <ref|worktree>`,
which stamps non-main provenance, and the next commit to main replaces it.
There is no debounce: a commit is atomic and already quiet. autoPublishDebounceSec
was deleted with the four other guards that existed only to make an mtime
comparison behave -- that comparison looped 64 times in one afternoon.
//compressors: Selective compression (§5): warm Haiku sessions that turn each turn-final into one
short readable line. ON BY DEFAULT (the operator's standing instruction: 'it should
just be on'); 2 is the smallest pool that is not a serialization point; 0 turns it
off and panes show the agent's full text. The acceptance suites stay model-free
anyway: they run with DODONA_NO_AUTOSTART=1, which also skips warming the pool, and
the compression suite uses the fake agent as a deterministic compressor.
//permissions: Lanes run bypassPermissions by default — the same permissiveness the operator's IDE
grants in auto mode. A lane cannot ask: headless -p has no prompt channel, so
anything not pre-approved is denied outright and the agent strands mid-task (it
edits fine, then cannot build what it edited). Measured: PreToolUse hooks STILL fire
under bypassPermissions, so the claim gate keeps bounding ticket lanes and the
merge-time backstop still refuses out-of-claim diffs. Set permissionMode to
'acceptEdits' plus an allowedTools list for a repo you would rather keep on a leash.
